title: Trade Surveillance Review
summary: Reconstruct order lifecycles, distinguish cancellations from executions, compare activity with aligned market benchmarks, and evaluate manipulation indicators as leads for human review.
audience: Trade-surveillance analysts, market-conduct reviewers, and surveillance-control testers
decision: Which order or execution patterns warrant further human review after sequence, ownership, market context, and denominator checks?
report_sections: Limitations, negative controls, and human decision

findings.title: A cancellation follows an opposite-side fill and warrants review
findings.detail: O1 cancels 800 of 1000 shares 300 ms after O2 fills 100 shares on the opposite side. The authored screen matches; intent and causation are not established.
findings.recommendation: Review broader patterns, market context, and strategy rationale through the authorized surveillance process.

findings.title: A high cancellation ratio has a supported context and no opposite fill
findings.detail: O3 cancels 500 shares after a documented quote change. No opposite-side execution exists in the complete supplied window.
findings.recommendation: Retain the negative scenario result and bounded ordinary explanation; do not infer manipulation from cancellation alone.

findings.title: One same-owner execution requires control and strategy context
findings.detail: O4 and O5 represent two account-side legs of one 100-share execution between confirmed same-owner accounts. No intent or broader pattern is established.
findings.recommendation: Review strategy independence, controls, repetition, and beneficial-ownership evidence; do not call the observation illegal wash trading.

conclusion: Two surveillance leads warrant contextual human review: A has a cancellation following an opposite-side fill, and C has one same-owner execution. B is a complete negative for the sequence screen; the example establishes no manipulation, intent, or illegal wash trading.
report_narrative: Two surveillance leads warrant contextual human review: A has a cancellation following an opposite-side fill, and C has one same-owner execution. B is a complete negative for the sequence screen; the example establishes no manipulation, intent, or illegal wash trading.

Five accepted orders reconcile to eleven canonical event messages and three unique executions. The reconstruction preserves message sequence, order-state transitions, linked fill legs and benchmark coverage before applying fictional screens.
TS-F01: O1 cancels 800 of 1000 shares 300 ms after O2 fills 100 shares on the opposite side. The authored screen matches; intent and causation are not established.
TS-F02: O3 cancels 500 shares after a documented quote change. No opposite-side execution exists in the complete supplied window.
TS-F03: O4 and O5 represent two account-side legs of one 100-share execution between confirmed same-owner accounts. No intent or broader pattern is established.

Every order lifecycle reconciles accepted quantity to filled, cancelled and residual quantities as specified in file 10. Duplicate message captures do not create additional orders, and two sides of one execution do not create two executions.

Account A has a cancellation following an opposite-side fill; C has one same-owner execution. These are two contextual review leads. B is a complete negative for the sequence screen; none of the screens establishes intent, manipulation or illegal wash trading.

The fictional event ledger, execution links and scenario criteria provide the calculation basis. FINRA, CFTC and SEC references retain their market and jurisdictional scope rather than converting the example screen into a legal test.

Obtain relevant strategy, ownership, communications and market context through the authorized surveillance process. Challenge legitimate explanations and benchmark gaps before any reviewer disposition.
